data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Resilience is not a property of centralization vs. decentralization, but of the 'Entropy of Configuration'; a centralized system can be more resilient if it intentionally simulates 'organic' messiness.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The coordination layer (the 'brain' of the large service) remains a single point of failure regardless of node diversity.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The complexity of managing synthetic diversity introduces new, non-linear failure modes (version-mismatch bugs).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"By employing 'Synthetic Diversity'\u2014intentionally deploying different versions of software, different timeout settings, and randomized resource limits across its redundant nodes\u2014a large service can decouple its failure modes while maintaining the coordination benefits of a single operator, effectively 'outrunning' the correlated failure risk of both models.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
